title: Common kernel definitions
description: Shared identifier, actor and enum definitions. Every other kernel schema references these so the vocabulary cannot drift between contracts.

agentId.description: An agent identifier. Deliberately a pattern rather than an enum: a 104-agent roster cannot live in a schema enum without every staffing change becoming a schema change. The closed set is enforced instead by KernelCrossCheckTests against the registry, which also catches ids referenced but never defined.

agentTier.description: ceo reports to the founder; boss runs a division; specialist does the work.

modelTier.description: Which model an agent runs on. This is a cost control, not a preference: at the studio's ceiling an Opus task costs roughly ten times a batched Haiku one, so the default is haiku and anything above it must earn its place.

currency.description: Always stated explicitly. An unlabelled '300' was read as USD when it meant DKK, a tenfold error that reached a committed budget file before anyone noticed.

actorId.description: Anything that can act: an agent, the founder, or automated CI.

decisionLevel.description: L0 constitution (human only) through L4 tuning (balance simulator).

evidenceTier.description: T0 static through T5 human playtest.

retryBudget.description: Capped at 3 by the architecture: after three failed attempts an agent must escalate with a hypothesis rather than keep guessing.
